answer: An identity-scoped bond with a long unlock window blocks Sybil attacks. Each new agent must post stake that is slashed outright on proven collusion and returns only after review, so one attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across thousands of addresses. Forging N clones costs N bonds and slashing risk, and each address needs its own mined nonce, forcing the attacker to wander through proof-of-work and pay real electricity per clone. A patient falcon hunting one target beats mass-produced fakes; honest agents stay distinct like ivory, and the attack turns unprofitable well below quorum.
